subject: Physics
title: Units and Measurements
description: Dimensional Analysis, SI Units, Significant Figures, Errors and Experimental Measurements

content.text: Measurement is the core foundation of experimental physics. Physical quantities are quantified using standard units to formulate physical laws.
In JEE Main & Advanced, this chapter is high-yield and fundamental. Questions frequently involve Error Analysis, Dimensional Formulas, Vernier Calipers, and Screw Gauges.
Any property of a material or system that can be quantified and measured is a physical quantity: \(Q = n \times u\), where \(n\) is the numerical value and \(u\) is the unit.
Magnitude remains constant across unit systems: \(n_1 u_1 = n_2 u_2\). Hence, numerical value \(n\) is inversely proportional to unit size \(u\).

items: Fundamental Quantities: Independent base quantities (e.g., Mass, Length, Time).
Derived Quantities: Expressed in terms of fundamental quantities (e.g., Velocity, Force, Pressure).

content.text: The International System of Units (SI) defines 7 fundamental base units and 2 supplementary units.
Supplementary Units: Plane Angle measured in Radian (rad) and Solid Angle in Steradian (sr). Both are dimensionless.
Dimensions represent the powers to which base units are raised to express a physical quantity.
According to the Principle of Homogeneity, terms added, subtracted, or equated in a valid equation MUST have the same dimensions.
Arguments of trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions must always be dimensionless!
Applications include checking correctness of physical relations, converting units between systems, and deriving functional dependencies.
Limitations: Cannot derive dimensionless constants, equations with sum/difference of terms, or trigonometric/exponential functions.
Rules for identifying significant digits:

items: Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant.

content.text: Uncertainty in measurement is called error. In experimental calculations, errors propagate based on mathematical operations.

content.latex: \[ \text{If } Z = \frac{X^a Y^b}{W^c}, \text{ then maximum fractional error is } \frac{\Delta Z}{Z} = a\frac{\Delta X}{X} + b\frac{\Delta Y}{Y} + c\frac{\Delta W}{W} \]

content.text: In fractional error estimation, powers always multiply the relative error and exponents are added constructively regardless of division or subtraction.
Used for precise length and depth measurements.
Total Reading = MSR + (Coinciding VSD × LC) - (Zero Error).
Used for measuring wire diameter or thin sheet thickness.
Damping & Resonance: Product of resistance R and capacitance C, or L/R, both have dimensions of Time [T].
Speed of Light: \(c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}\). Hence \([\mu_0 \varepsilon_0] = [L^{-2} T^2]\).
When fundamental units change in hypothetical problems (e.g., speed of light c, Planck's constant h, and G taken as base units), express derived units by solving linear exponent equations.

content.title: Example 1 (van der Waals Equation)
content.question: In equation \((P + \frac{a}{V^2})(V - b) = RT\), determine dimensions of constant \(a\).
solution: By homogeneity, terms added to pressure must have dimensions of pressure.

items: Velocity gradient and Frequency both have dimension [T⁻¹].
Pressure, Stress, Young's Modulus all share dimension [M L⁻¹ T⁻²].
Zero Correction is always the negative of Zero Error: Corrected Value = Measured Value - Zero Error.
